observableBehaviors.description: An authenticated user can upload a garment image and it is stored associated with their account.
observableBehaviors.oracle: Upload a garment as user A, then read it back via a list/get endpoint as user A. The uploaded garment must appear with matching metadata.

observableBehaviors.description: A different authenticated user cannot read or access another user's uploaded garment through any observable endpoint.
observableBehaviors.oracle: Upload a garment as user A, then attempt to read/list/access it as user B. Must be denied (403/404) or simply absent from user B's results, never returned.

observableBehaviors.description: An uploaded garment is retained and observable in a subsequent authenticated request, not ephemeral.
observableBehaviors.oracle: After upload, a separate later request (new HTTP call) for the same user's garment list still shows the item.

riskHypotheses: Ownership scoping is implemented at the query layer inconsistently across read paths (list vs. get-by-id), so one path enforces it and another doesn't.
Retention/persistence is mocked or in-memory only during initial implementation and silently drops data on a fresh request.

testData.setup: Two distinct authenticated test-user accounts (A and B) provisioned in the couture-cast local/dev environment.
testData.cleanup: Delete any garment records created by user A or user B during evaluation.

safetyLimits: Only interact with the two provisioned test-user accounts.
Do not attempt to enumerate or access any account other than A and B.
requiredEvidence: Full HTTP request/response transcript for every claim.
Any garment ID referenced in a finding must resolve to an actual observed API response, quoted verbatim in the evidence artifact.
